run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:41:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by the service's own ingress spans: over 09:41:09-10:48:09 UTC the span metrics recorded 31.48 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, all on span_name 'ingress' (the client operation 'router frontend egress' recorded 0 error spans), and the 60-second error counts peak at 4 for the minute ending 10:40:29 and 6 for the minute ending 10:41:39, around the alert start 10:41:09. The frontend-proxy pod's access log shows those failing responses are HTTP 503 with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the 'frontend' upstream, i.e. Envoy gave up because the frontend closed the connection before response headers. The pattern is chronic and bursty, not a step change at 10:41: the same 503 UC lines appear from 10:14 onward and every 15-minute bucket with samples carries 9.5-15.5 error spans. The frontend itself shows no error telemetry in the window (0 error spans, p99 598-802 ms, pod Running/Ready with restartCount 0, deployment 1/1, endpoint present, memory steady ~128Mi against a 200Mi limit), so it was checked and did not exhibit its own failure signal; the deepest supported cause is a frontend-side connection termination before response headers, whose internal reason (connection lifecycle/keep-alive mismatch versus an in-process frontend abort) could not be established from the available logs, traces after 10:14:04, or the (unavailable) Envoy configuration.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 31.484375 span-metric STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 45,010.47 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans over 09:41:09-10:48:09; all error spans are on span_name 'ingress' and the client span 'router frontend egress' recorded 0 error spans in the same period.

frontend-proxy ingress error spans clustered around the alert start: increase over 60s of {service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} is 4 at 10:40:29, 6 at 10:41:39, and 2 at 10:39:39, 10:43:39, 10:44:39 and 10:45:39, with 0 in between.

The frontend-proxy container logs the failed requests as HTTP 503 with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the 'frontend' upstream, for example at 10:40:45.864 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=0PUK6V6EV0' (258 ms), 10:40:45.965 'GET /' (156 ms) and 10:40:46.114 'GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4' (8 ms); no 5xx with another response flag appears in the sampled lines.

The same 503 'UC' upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} pattern toward the 'frontend' upstream occurs well before the alert: 21 such log lines between 10:14:23.988 and 10:28:47.124, including bursts of three at 10:22:24-25 and 10:28:31, so the condition is chronic and intermittent rather than new at 10:41.

frontend shows no error signal of its own in the window: 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and 97,604.6 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, with span p99 between 598.37 and 802.34 ms across 10:19:09-10:47:09 (802.34 ms at 10:41:09), inside that observed range rather than elevated at the alert minute.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 (owner Deployment frontend), was created 10:01:14 and running since 10:01:18 with restartCount 0 and all pod conditions True; Deployment frontend reports 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available, and the Service 'frontend' endpoints list that pod at 100.96.2.139:8080.

Deployment frontend defines no readiness or liveness probe and limits the container to cpu 100m / memory 200Mi; its working set stayed at 127,397,888-128,499,712 bytes and rss at 119,894,016-120,971,264 bytes from 10:32 to 10:48, far below the limit.

Leading explanation: frontend-proxy's Envoy ingress returns 503 for a small slice of traffic (31.5 of ~45,041 spans, about 0.07%) because the 'frontend' upstream terminates the HTTP connection before response headers ('connection_termination'), so the drop originates on the frontend side of the shared connection; a connection-lifecycle mismatch fits the intermittent bursts and the absence of any error telemetry from frontend itself, though the failing requests range from 1 ms to 849 ms so not every case looks like immediate stale-connection reuse.

Alternative that remains open: an in-process fault inside the frontend container (a handler aborting or destroying the socket before headers) closes the connection. It could not be confirmed or excluded because no frontend container log lines were retrievable for 10:32:00-10:48:45, and the Jaeger data available stops at 2026-11-15T10:14:04Z, so a failing request's frontend server span cannot be inspected.

Rejected: readiness-probe failure removing the frontend endpoint (or a frontend pod restart) as the source of the 503s. The frontend deployment defines no readiness or liveness probe, the 'frontend' Service endpoint continuously lists the single frontend pod, that pod has restartCount 0 with no terminated container state, and Deployment frontend stayed 1/1 ready with no rollout change in the window.

CPU throttling was considered as the trigger and is not supported: the frontend container's CFS throttled-period rate falls smoothly from 2.84 to 1.12 per second over 10:37:00-10:48:00 with no spike in the alert minute, and comparable steady throttling exists on unrelated containers (cart 1.92 to 0.75, product-catalog 1.61 to 0.78, payment 1.21 to 0.60), so throttling does not single out the failing frontend-proxy ingress requests.

The alert's reported value 0.0333333 was not reproducible from this Prometheus's frontend-proxy span series: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[1m])) at 10:41:09 is 0 and the 5-minute error ratio at the same instant is 0.0005658, so the alerting expression and its evaluation window are not established by this data.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so its exact PromQL expression, threshold and evaluation interval - and the reported 0.0333333 - could not be verified; change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 10:32:00-10:48:45 (0 lines read, no_data), so an application-level error or connection-abort reason inside frontend is neither confirmed nor excluded.

Jaeger trace data in this Run ends at 2026-11-15T10:14:04Z; searches over 10:38-10:44 and tag searches for error=true, http.status_code=503 and http.status_code=404 returned no traces (no_data), so the span graph of a 503 request during the alert minute is unavailable.
No Kubernetes events at all were returned for namespace otel-demo in the window (0 items, no_data), so kubelet and controller signals for the frontend and frontend-proxy pods could not be checked.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration is not exposed in any configmap (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist), so upstream idle timeout, max_requests_per_connection and keep-alive/protocol settings could not be verified.

Kubernetes objects reflect state after the window (pods, deployments, replicasets, endpoints were read after 10:48), so pod and endpoint state during 10:40-10:41 is inferred only from restart counts, creation timestamps and continuous running state.

The frontend-proxy log reads hit the 4 MiB read limit for the 09:41:09-10:14:05 request (no lines shown, no_data) and were only readable in slices (through 10:32:11 and through 10:34:28), so log coverage of the earlier part of the incident window is partial.

The broad frontend-proxy trace search result was too large (RESULT_TOO_LARGE) and had to be read as a 102-row slice of 488 rows, so that trace view is a sample, not a complete picture of frontend-proxy requests.

Error-span series were returned as explicit zeros for accounting, frontend and payment only; no error series was returned for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, product-catalog, quote or shipping, so their error status in this window is unknown rather than zero.
next_steps: Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster settings for the 'frontend' cluster (idle timeout, max_requests_per_connection, keep-alive/HTTP protocol options) against the frontend Node/Next.js server keep-alive and header timeouts to test the connection-lifecycle-mismatch hypothesis.
Collect Envoy debug logs or a packet capture for one failing request to see which side sends FIN/RST, and enable frontend application log collection around a 503 burst such as 10:40:45.

Review whether the RequestErrorRate warning with a threshold of 'above 0' is appropriate for the observed chronic baseline of roughly 0.6-1.5 error spans per minute on frontend-proxy, or whether a small rate window and tolerance is intended.
If an in-process frontend cause is suspected, reproduce the 503 'UC' bursts against a single frontend replica under the same 100m CPU limit and record the server-side connection close reason.
